event.title: Capture of 'El Chapo Isidro' Triggers Violence in Sinaloa
event.canonical_title: Capture of 'El Chapo Isidro' Triggers Violence in Sinaloa
event.summary: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro' and one of the FBI's ten most wanted fugitives, was arrested by Mexican special forces in Sinaloa. His capture has led to a surge of violence in the region, including gunfire and burning vehicles, causing panic among civilians. The operation reportedly involved cooperation with US intelligence.

timeline.title: Capture of Cartel Leader 'El Chapo Isidro' Sparks Violence in Sinaloa
timeline.summary: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro' and one of the FBI's most wanted fugitives, was captured by Mexican special forces in Sinaloa during a military operation. Following his arrest, violence erupted in the region, resulting in at least 11 deaths, with reports of gunfire and chaos among civilians. The operation involved cooperation with US intelligence and included a shootout between security forces and armed members of his cartel.

event_overview.title: About Mexican Drug Cartels
event_overview.subject: Mexican Drug Cartels
event_overview.summary: The event concerns the Mexican military’s November 2026 capture of Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro,” following a U.S.-supported investigation, and the violence reported in Sinaloa during and after the operation. Meza-Flores had long been identified by U.S. authorities as an alleged senior figure in Sinaloa-based drug-trafficking networks and faced U.S. federal criminal charges.

facts.label: Capture
facts.value: The U.S. Department of Justice said Meza-Flores was captured by the Mexican military on November 20-21, 2026, after a Homeland Security Task Force investigation; Mexican forces carried out the arrest.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: The operation and ensuing unrest were centered in Sinaloa, a northwestern Mexican state; the Meza-Flores organization was previously described by the U.S. Treasury as operating from Guasave, Sinaloa.

facts.label: Identity and organization
facts.value: U.S. authorities identify Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores by the aliases “El Chapo Isidro,” “Chapo Isidro,” and “Chapito Isidro.” A 2019 Justice Department announcement described him as the alleged leader of the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organization, a major trafficking organization based in Sinaloa.

facts.label: U.S. criminal case
facts.value: A federal superseding indictment alleged that, from about January 2005 through November 2019, Meza-Flores conspired to distribute cocaine, methamphetamine, heroin, and marijuana for importation into the United States, and alleged firearms offenses. These were charges, not findings of guilt.

facts.label: Cartel classification in U.S. policy
facts.value: The Justice Department states that the U.S. Secretary of State designated the Sinaloa Cartel as a Foreign Terrorist Organization and a Specially Designated Global Terrorist on February 20, 2025; this is a U.S. legal designation and does not itself determine individual criminal liability.

event_overview.scope_note: This timeline covers the November 2026 capture and immediate violence in Sinaloa, not the full history of the Sinaloa Cartel, the Beltrán Leyva network, or every related prosecution and security operation.
